articles.title: US Aviation System Failure Grounds Flights Nationwide
articles.summary: A failure in the US aviation communications system grounded flights across the country, affecting about 12,000 flights; officials apologized for the disruption.
articles.detail: Reports show that a system equipment failure at the US Federal Aviation Administration triggered a nationwide ground stop. Around 3,500 aircraft were in the air at the time, and air traffic controllers guided all planes to land safely. Officials said 12,000 flights were affected and could not be recovered, and apologized to the public. A Chinese passenger diverted to Mexico recalled the tense moments. US authorities said no evidence of malicious activity has been found and are investigating the contractor's responsibility.
articles.impact: The mass grounding exposes the aging state of aviation communications infrastructure and could spur equipment upgrades and regulatory scrutiny.

articles.title: US Transportation Department Pushes Air Traffic Control Modernization
articles.summary: The US Transportation Department says 69% of aging air traffic control communications equipment has been replaced, and it is seeking Congressional funding to advance system modernization.
articles.detail: Sources show that US Transportation Secretary Duffy said about 69% of outdated air traffic control communications equipment has been replaced, with some units in service for 30 years and in urgent need of upgrades. He said the department is investigating whether contractor L3Harris should be held responsible for technical failures, and will partner with AT&T, Verizon and Lumen to develop a new communications architecture. US officials say air traffic has fully resumed operations.
articles.impact: Urgent demand for air traffic control infrastructure upgrades could drive growth in related communications and aviation equipment orders.
